profile.headline: Infrastructure engineer, aka Terraform mechanic | Kubernetes on AWS, Spacelift, platform engineering | 11 years in architectural lighting | Embedded and home-automation tinkerer
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I'm an infrastructure engineer, or as I like to put it, a Terraform mechanic. I like investigating infrastructure-as-code problems, and I don't stop at “it just fails sometimes.”
At Flatiron Health I work on the platform: Terraform/OpenTofu and Spacelift, Kubernetes (EKS) on AWS, GitLab CI/CD, and the identity and access wiring between them. I turn recurring problems into modules, policies, self-serve paths and docs.
Before software, I spent 11 years designing architectural lighting in New York and Guadalajara, for corporate campuses, fashion boutiques, international retail rollouts, and private homes. I wrote specifications others built from, integrated lighting and control systems with each other and with the space, and verified that what got built matched the spec. The part I enjoyed most was iterating with clients and seeing it through on site. I keep being surprised by how much of that shows up in software engineering. Maybe it was always the same craft, just with different materials.
I studied mechatronics engineering and still tinker with hardware: bare-metal C on STM32 boards, and Arduino and Raspberry Pi prototypes. I also run my home automation on Home Assistant. Making systems work together is the thread through all of it, and I'm especially interested in lighting technology, home and building automation, and connected devices.
Craftsmanship is personal for me: I enjoy the small details, and building systems that explain themselves.

positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States

positions.title: Software Engineer, Platform
positions.description:
• Terraform Enterprise → Spacelift: built the infrastructure as code that bootstraps and manages our Spacelift platform, including a seed workspace that creates the administrative layers, layered access (GitLab code ownership, Spacelift spaces and SAML groups), and a bootstrapping path with minimal dependencies.
• Self-service stacks: co-wrote an abstraction that lets teams declare their Terraform stacks, spaces and worker roles in YAML. Changes are checked in CI, and stacks are built within the platform's rules.
• Worker identity: helped build the worker modules that give each space, project or group a set of roles with standard policies, so self-hosted workers in one AWS account can authenticate to many. Recommended moving workers from IRSA to OIDC trust in each stack's identity, and helped close a legacy path to a broad admin role without breaking legacy workloads.
• GitLab integration: reproduced Terraform Enterprise's push-triggered behavior in Spacelift's policy layer; my trigger policy is now the default for all GitLab-backed stacks.
• Jenkins retirement: moved AWS IAM and identity automation to native Spacelift stacks after working out why the old design existed (clone load, account ordering), preserving its behavior exactly.
• Reliability and testing: tuned self-hosted worker pools with a year of run data, traced recurring CI failures on EKS to several interacting causes, and rebuilt shared module tests to run against the branch under review.
• Fleet changes with AI: rolled out CoreStack across 20 EKS clusters in under two weeks, with a Claude Code planning agent directing subagents; built the organization's Terraform/Spacelift assistant in Slack.
• Design and support: led the design of delegated access for regional SRE teams; write the proposals and reference docs that settle designs before implementation; go-to expert in help channels for Terraform, Spacelift, EKS and CI/CD.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Launch Automation
positions.description:
• Golden paths: contributed to the standard path for deploying containers to self-managed EKS (default Helm chart, GitLab CI/CD templates, review apps), working mainly on the runner, cluster-authentication and secrets pieces.
• GitLab Runner module: owned the initial development of a Terraform module that deploys and configures many runner instances across clusters, with a Vault sidecar for deployment-time secrets, live tests that deploy a runner, run a job on it and tear it down, and automated releases. Adopted by multiple business units.
• Multi-architecture CI: added x86-64 and ARM64 support for runner managers and jobs, and built multi-architecture CI images that let pipelines run on lower-cost ARM64 instances.
• Metrics footprint: deployed Kubecost on a minimal Prometheus configuration that needed no long-term metric storage, and built Datadog dashboards that let teams right-size their workloads.

positions.title: Software Engineering Apprentice
positions.description:
Moved from lighting design into DevOps, learning containers and CI/CD on production work.
• Built the base CI job image and its build pipeline, which became the foundation for the GitLab Runner module I went on to own.
• Led the first end-to-end deployment pipeline running entirely on ARM64.

positions.title: Senior Lighting Designer
positions.description:
• Led design and specification for 15+ projects, including Silicon Valley corporate campuses under Bjarke Ingels Group and Heatherwick Studio, luxury fashion boutiques, and a 34-store NARS Cosmetics rollout across Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
• Selected and specified lighting and control systems, matching dimming technologies (phase, 0–10V, DMX, wireless) to each project's control system, level of integration and use, and resolved integration issues through mockups and field tests.
• Developed custom fixtures with architects and manufacturers, improving optical performance and mounting for aesthetic and constructive integration.
• Kept specifications with hundreds of line items consistent across years of revisions, using templates, checks and standards that carried each change through schedules, cut sheets, details and drawings. Looking back, it was my first taste of infrastructure as code.
• Reviewed contractor submittals and installations against the specification; led and mentored teams of 2–4 designers.

positions.title: Lighting Designer

Designed lighting for high-end residential, hospitality, corporate and cultural projects with leading Mexican architects; several were featured in architecture and design publications.
• Specified LED and digital controls through the industry's transition, and helped the team adopt and specify the new technology.
• Analyzed electrical loads, usage patterns and controls for energy savings.
• Known for clear, high-quality documentation.
